lessons: Stranded picks: Tribute to Hunger and Typhoid Rats at picks 2-3 never reached my WR deck, so commit to a pair by mid pack 1 as the guide says.

Tonight contradicted the guide's 55% WR figure: my 0-3 WR with Voiceless Spirit, Spectral Rider, Falkenrath Marauders and Scourge of Geier Reach lost in 13-24 turn games, so fliers alone still failed.
Keep a second removal spell over a second Unruly Mob, as the guide advises, because my WR lost to WU and BR games where ground filler could not close.
Draft white-based fliers and humans with removal like Claustrophobia and Smite the Monstrous; this WU list went 3-0 and never dropped a game, with Galvanic Juggernaut as colourless top end.
Cut weak one-drops like Delver of Secrets and the weak auras, then run 17 lands with a Plains-heavy split (9 Plains, 8 Island) to match white's depth; this build went 6-0 in games.
Take colourless playables like Galvanic Juggernaut early as a hedge, since it was second pick of pack one and stayed in the final deck while off-colour cards were cut.
Keep Moonmist over an extra filler body: our BG deck lost 0-2 to WU fliers (Stitched Drake, Abbey Griffin) with few answers, confirming the guide that fliers win.
Black-green held up: Dead Weight, Corpse Lunge, Moan of the Unhallowed and Morkrut Banshee backed a 2-1 match record, so black is a safe anchor when blue and red are thin.
Sideboarding Maw of the Mire and Mulch in for Moldgraf Monstrosity and Moon Heron preceded my 2-1 win over white-red, so keep cheap interaction flexible against Brimstone Volley and Unruly Mob.
Lost 0-2 to black-green in a 34-turn grind, so favour evasive threats like Murder of Crows over extra ground blockers when the board stalls.
My first pick Sever the Bloodline and Trepanation Blade went unplayed; green-blue creatures like Lumberknot and Makeshift Mauler were the cards that made the deck, so commit to that lane sooner.
Where tonight contradicted the guide: WU, called average and slow, was the table's only 3-0 deck and beat my WR 2-0 in 13 and 26 turns, so do not dismiss it.
The three-flier rule held: my WR had only two Chapel Geist, Midnight Haunting and Spectral Rider in the air and lost a 26-turn game, so take a third flier over ground filler.
The guide's WR core worked: cheap white creatures plus Rebuke, Smite the Monstrous and Brimstone Volley took a 2-1 over RG, and Chapel Geist and Midnight Haunting beat Silverchase Fox.
Self-mill UB with Death's Hold and Lost in the Mist as top end was too slow: both 1-2 losses ran 17–23 turns, so prioritise cheap early pressure like Falkenrath Noble.
Delver of Secrets // Insectile Aberration was taken twice (pack 1 pick 9, pack 3 pick 14) and never played; late picks should go to two-drops and playable Skaab bodies instead.
I took the second Curse of the Bloody Tome and cut it anyway; a cheap creature from that slot would have helped the curve in both 1-2 losses.
Fliers win this format, as the guide says: my RG deck had only two Orchard Spirits for evasion and lost 1-2 to UG's Moon Heron and Murder of Crows; take fliers over ground fatties.
Tricks mattered more than the guide implies: I ran one Ranger's Guile and no Moment of Heroism, so WR's two Rebukes and Smite the Monstrous left my ground werewolves unprotected.
I spent three picks on Gatstaf Shepherd and took Festerhide Boar, which the guide calls filler; take a flier or cheap removal over those late picks.
Draft enough removal and evasive top-end before filler: my BR deck's Dead Weight, Geistflame, Harvest Pyre and Corpse Lunge could not stop 19-24 turn stalls against RG and UB, losing 0-2 each.
Don't spend mid-pack picks on off-colour cards like Curiosity or Spare from Evil; my BR deck's cheap creatures carried a 2-1 win over WR, so commit to a two-colour creature curve sooner.
